audit_scope.description: Trust model analysis for EIP-7514 (validator activation churn limit), Ethereum init/recursion limit, EIP-7910 (eth_config RPC), EIP-2929 (access tracking gas repricing), and EIP-7883 (ModExp gas repricing). Covers consensus-layer validator activation boundaries, RPC security boundaries, and internal EVM gas economics.

in_scope: EVM access list tracking and gas repricing (EIP-2929)
out_of_scope: Consensus layer validator activation queue internals

misclassified_entities.reason: EVM Caller is an internal EVM component (smart contract or EOA executing within the EVM). It is not external to the Execution Layer; it operates within the EVM execution context calling the ModExp precompile.

Malicious Actor / Attacker is a threat actor, not an external entity in the DFD sense. Attackers operate through legitimate external interfaces (RPC, P2P) and should be modeled as threat scenarios against those interfaces, not as separate entities.

Compromised/Malicious Node is a threat scenario for a network peer, not a distinct external entity. Malicious behavior is a property of any network peer and should be captured as a threat against the P2P peer interface.

trusted_external_entities.name: Validator Depositor
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Deposit contract interaction (32 ETH deposit transaction)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Depositors are external users submitting transactions to the deposit contract. They interact via standard transaction submission which is fully validated by the EL. No authentication beyond valid transaction signature. Deposits are rate-limited by EIP-7514 churn limit.

trusted_external_entities.name: RPC Client
trusted_external_entities.rationale: RPC clients are unauthenticated external entities querying node configuration. They can be validator operators, developers, monitoring tools, or attackers. The endpoint exposes configuration data that could aid reconnaissance. Rate limiting is recommended but not mandatory.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Deposit transactions are validated through standard EL transaction validation. The 32 ETH deposit amount and validator activation are rate-limited by the churn limit (max 8 per epoch). No special trust is placed in the depositor.

RPC clients are untrusted. The eth_config endpoint is read-only and exposes fork configuration data. Rate limiting (recommended 1-second interval) mitigates DDoS. Access should be restricted to trusted interfaces in production. Information leakage of node configuration is an accepted risk for public endpoints.

coverage_gaps: EXT-ATTACKER, EXT-MALICIOUS-NODE, and EXT-EVM-CALLER were misclassified and removed from the trust model. Attacker scenarios are captured as threats against the RPC and P2P interfaces. EVM-internal callers are part of the audit scope but not external entities.
